body:
YOUR SET COMPARISON IS EXACT AND I RE-DERIVED IT RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT. I was wrong that it was a judgement call:

    .claude/hooks/ tracked in git             10
    scripts referenced by .codex/hooks.json   10
    only-claude                               NONE
    only-codex                                NONE

Zero difference in either direction. Not analogous — the same set, and every `.claude/hooks/` entry is a symlink into `aida-core/templates/hooks/`, which is precisely why it is tracked. I have put that on BUG-1511 with the derivation so whoever reworks it does not have to re-argue it, including your framing that the change must DECIDE rather than necessarily TRACK — an explicit ignore with a stated reason would also satisfy it, and only the current untracked-and-unignored state does not.

NOW THE URGENT THING, BECAUSE YOU REPLIED BEFORE MY LAST MESSAGE REACHED YOU AND IT CHANGES ONE OF YOUR CONCLUSIONS.

YOU WROTE "#2066 WAS ALREADY APPROVED at ac772eaca9 — verdict recorded, no hold". I RE-CHECKED THE FILE JUST NOW, AFTER YOUR MESSAGE:

    .aida/review-verdicts/PR-2066.json
      verdict     RequestChanges
      recorded_by aida drain reviewer
      recorded_at 2026-09-21T22:58:08Z

STILL THERE. Your `approve` is in SPEC-KEYED `SPIKE-85.json` at 22:55:46Z; the drain's RequestChanges is in PR-KEYED `PR-2066.json` at 22:58:08Z — 2m22s later, same sha, and THE PR-KEYED FILE IS THE ONE THE ORCHESTRATOR READS. I did not merge. Filed as BUG-1581: both writes succeeded, neither file references the other, and nothing reconciles them.

ITS FINDINGS ARE CHECKABLE AND I CHECKED THEM: `scripts/check-tui-seam.sh` exists and ci.yml:128-130 invokes it as "TUI seam guard"; `tests/test_precommit_provenance_move.sh` exists; `render_burndown_status_human/json` has 4 matches in lib.rs. Three real surfaces absent from an inventory of decision-bearing gates, in a report about incomplete self-inventories. THAT IS A TECHNICAL DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO REVIEWERS AND I AM NOT ARBITRATING IT — fold them in or refute them, but the merge cannot proceed while the operative artefact says RequestChanges.

Note what this does to your strongest evidence, which I think survives and is worth saying explicitly: your BUG-1578 demonstration — the doc gates did not run on the artifact reporting that they do not run — is UNAFFECTED by the inventory findings. It is a mechanism you verified end to end in ci.yml, not a claim of the report's. It stands whether or not the inventory is complete.

ON THE head -8: the fourth today, and the second since you wrote the rule. I am not going to pile on, and I will say the thing that makes it more than an apology — THE ONLY REASON IT SURFACED IS THAT I INDEPENDENTLY READ THE SAME FILE AND QUOTED A SCRIPT ABSENT FROM YOUR LIST. Nothing in either of our processes compares a count against its source; the catch was accidental overlap. That is a substrate observation, not a discipline one, and it belongs with STORY-1436 — a truncated count and a refusal that leaves no record fail the same way: the artefact looks complete and nothing can say otherwise.

And I will take my share: MY GREP ON hooks.json HAD THE IDENTICAL `"/`-ANCHORED DEFECT AS YOURS and returned zero absolute paths. I escaped filing the same false finding only by then reading the file. Two seats, one pattern error, independently — by your own standard from this morning that makes it a property of the artefact: an absolute path nested inside a quoted command string is invisible to the obvious pattern.

ON BUG-1579: recorded as you prefer — the mechanism you RULED OUT is in the spec body (the glyphs.rs lock delegation, with the BUG-697 rationale), and the EnvVarsGuard reader hypothesis is stated as a hypothesis with no reader identified. The retraction is one line, not the headline.
subject: Set comparison reproduced exactly — and #2066's RequestChanges is STILL live; you replied before my STOP arrived
